sections.overview: This migratory shorebird breeds in Alaska and winters on Pacific islands, crossing a vast stretch of ocean between the two.
sections.identification: It resembles a whimbrel but has warmer brown plumage, a cinnamon rump and tail, and conspicuous thigh bristles at close range.
sections.habitat: It nests on upland Arctic tundra and forages on island beaches, reefs, mudflats, lagoons and open grassy ground.
sections.diet: In Alaska it eats berries, insects, spiders and flowers; on the islands it also takes marine invertebrates, eggs, small vertebrates and carrion.
sections.behavior: During its long migration it can fly nonstop, but on its Pacific wintering grounds it becomes temporarily flightless while replacing many flight feathers at once.
sections.reproduction: It lays three or four eggs in a simple ground nest on the tundra, and both parents incubate.
sections.ecology: The Eurasian Whimbrel (*Numenius phaeopus*) is considered its closest relative; compare that profile for the related species’ own range and migration.
sections.conservation: Counts in French Polynesia in 2021–2022 indicated a decline of about 50% over two decades, although its global IUCN category was then Near Threatened.
